On the record: Lead sponsor. Posts almost daily: "We need to pass this bill to get our country back to building." Promotes CEA and McKinsey savings estimates.

"Data center owners should pay for their electricity and any grid upgrades, not you. Our new permitting reform bill makes that mandatory." His office says "negotiations continue" on the NHPA tribal consultation language. Facing home-state pressure from Rep. Stansbury, Deb Haaland, and tribes. Nov. 3, to ENR: the bill "will help us get to 'yes' or 'no' on energy projects faster, while protecting important environmental safeguards." Nov. 4, after the election, on calls to wait: "I'm not going to wait," calling this "the closest we have come to actually finding something that can get signed into law." Nov. 5: "Americans spoke clearly this week that they want their elected representatives focused on affordability... Let's get it done and pass BAAJA."
"We want to make it easier in America to build things." On X: "There is no negotiating with the anti-growth Left." Cites the White House CEA estimate of $250 a year in bill savings.

Sponsor, but sets a condition for his own caucus: "regulatory misbehavior against clean energy does need to be resolved before Democrats will vote for this bill" (Oct. 19). On Oct. 29: "We await real signs of regulatory good faith." Also: "BAAJA is our best bet to lower people's electricity costs." Nov. 2, at a Rhode Island event: Democrats should not wait, because "a bird in the hand" may not be there next year (Punchbowl, Nov. 3). Same day, at a Pawtucket roundtable with NAM and LIUNA: the administration "must now end their mischief and show some real regulatory good faith." Nov. 4, after the election: "It's a bird in the hand. We'd be fools not to take it," adding that "there's no guarantee Congress would ever find another compromise that would be able to pass the Senate." Nov. 5, responding to Jeffries: "The EPW & ENR Committees have actively solicited input from many House members as BAAJA was negotiated and after it was introduced," and he hopes the manager's amendment addresses "many concerns."
"Really, really meaningful permitting reform, all the way across the board." Agencies can't walk back permits "without being liable for the damages."
"The bipartisan permitting bill will unlock critical infrastructure projects – from roads & bridges to energy." Commends Capito's leadership (EPW member).

Says Democrats should pass BAAJA now rather than wait for a better deal: "Six months from now, after a [possible] impeachment, maybe [the White House] won't be willing to negotiate, or maybe we get too close to an election and Vance doesn't want to negotiate, right? So why not take this win now?" Quoted by a reporter; brackets are the reporter's.

"To help make life more affordable, we need permitting reform... EPW's bipartisan bill cuts through the bureaucracy." Held a permitting roundtable with Barrasso. He also sponsored the separate Ratepayer Protection Act, which failed 57-43. Lost his Nov. 3 race to Sherrod Brown (AP); still a senator for the Nov. 9 vote.

Nov. 7: "Now is the time to get permitting reform across the finish line during the lame-duck session" (the posts do not name BAAJA). Oct. 1, the day after introduction: "We need clear approval timelines and legal certainty for approved projects. We must pass" permitting reform. He introduced his own permitting bill in May.
